NEW DELHI: China on Monday said it was ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries, amid reports of a slowdown in visa issuance to Indian nationals."China issues visas for eligible foreign nationals coming to China in accordance with laws and regulations," a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said in a written response to questions from news agency PTI."We stand ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel of both sides," the spokesperson added.The remarks come amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals, including business travellers.According to PTI, fewer Indian businessmen were reportedly granted visas to attend this month's China International Import Expo in Shanghai. The annual trade fair provides a platform for businesses from around the world to showcase their products to Chinese consumers.Beijing has also stopped the China Visa Application Centre, a service provider, from accepting visa applications, with Chinese diplomatic missions now handling them directly amid rising demand for visas, particularly business visas.Visa arrangements between the two countries have improved since India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years. The move was part of efforts to repair bilateral ties, which came under severe strain following the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.The resumption of tourist visas was seen as a significant step towards normalising relations after years of strained ties.As part of efforts to ease travel, the two countries also resumed direct air connectivity between several cities, including the Beijing-New Delhi route.According to Indian officials, the visa rejection rate for Chinese nationals has come down to around seven per cent in recent months to encourage business and tourism-related travel to India.China, meanwhile, launched the "China Online Visa Application System" for Indian applicants in December last year, allowing them to apply for visas online.Responding to a question on the status of bilateral relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi in September this year, the spokesperson said Beijing was ready to work with New Delhi to strengthen ties."The most important common understanding they (PM Modi and Xi) reached is that China and India need to be partners. Both sides are working to deliver on this important common understanding."China stands ready to work with India to improve and grow bilateral relations, support each other's development and revitalisation, and contribute to world peace and prosperity," the spokesperson said.
Article Summary: China says it is ready to work with India to facilitate visa arrangements for business personnel from both countries. Comments come amid reports that Chinese diplomatic missions have reduced visa issuance to Indian nationals. India resumed issuing tourist visas to Chinese nationals in July last year after a gap of five years.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Sunday backed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's criticism of corporate leaders for failing to pass on the benefits of reduced corporate taxes to employees through higher salaries and increased hiring.However, he also used the Prime Minister's remarks to take digs at the government over the employment situation, regulatory hurdles and corruption.Reacting to the Prime Minister's remarks, Tharoor said PM Modi had a point in arguing that the government had lowered corporate taxes to encourage companies to invest, create jobs and raise salaries, but businesses had not fulfilled their part of the bargain.“I think what the Prime Minister said is a reality. The corporates may have their own defence of it, but his argument, as I understand it, is that the government has lowered taxes to encourage companies to invest more, create more jobs, and raise salaries, and the companies have not kept their share of the bargain,” Tharoor said.He pointed to the difficulties faced by job seekers, particularly fresh graduates, saying the public had repeatedly raised concerns about the lack of employment opportunities.Citing reports of an IIT graduate failing to secure a placement, he said such instances, which were rarely heard of in the past, suggested that the employment environment for college graduates was “rather grim”.Tharoor also called for simpler regulations and improvements in the ease of doing business, while alleging that corruption had worsened and urging the government to pay greater attention to the economy.“The economy requires attention, and if the Prime Minister is pointing fingers at the companies and the companies want to point fingers at government policies, that's something we can watch,” he said.“We do believe there are things the government could be doing better. They could certainly be simplifying regulations; ease of doing business is not a reality. And I'm sorry to say that corruption, according to every businessman I speak to, is much worse than it's ever been,” he added.Taking a swipe at the government's anti-corruption slogan, Tharoor said, “And this is something which, honestly, the Prime Minister had famously said: 'Na khaunga, na khane dunga.' And now we realize he only meant beef.”Tharoor's remarks came after PM Modi, addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) annual general meeting on Thursday, criticised industry leaders for not translating the benefits of corporate tax cuts into higher employee salaries or additional jobs.Recalling that the basic corporate tax rate had been reduced from 30 per cent in 2014 to 22 per cent, the Prime Minister questioned whether companies had increased salaries or expanded their workforce following the tax relief.“I know you will not clap. I know that very well, because your appetite is so enormous that no matter how much you are given, it is never enough (aapki bhookh itni hai, kitna hi khilao pet bharta hi nahi),” he told the gathering.“Did you increase the salaries of your employees? Did you increase the number of employees? No. The attitude remains: 'Modiji, you do it, we will see',” he said.The Prime Minister also cited the income-tax exemption for individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh annually, saying the relief had boosted people's purchasing power and consumption. He referred to the government's reduction of GST rates on several products and faster income-tax refunds, which he said had freed up money that would otherwise have remained tied up for months.The remarks came amid fresh demands from the corporate sector for tax concessions in the upcoming Union Budget, with business leaders having submitted their wish list to the finance minister.While highlighting measures taken by the government to improve the business environment, the Prime Minister urged industry leaders to openly suggest further reforms and assured them that the government was willing to consider their proposals.“I have come because I respect you. But your experience with previous govts has been so bitter that I am paying the price for it. This is not that old govt. This is a friendly govt... Without hesitation and without inhibition, write to me openly and tell me what reforms are still needed,” he said.Recalling an interaction with Income Tax Department officials in Gujarat around 2001-02, when he was the chief minister, Modi said he had questioned the approach of treating taxpayers as potential wrongdoers.The Prime Minister also invoked Mahatma Gandhi's message of Swadeshi and self-reliance, questioning why industry leaders still needed to be reminded of the importance of promoting indigenous products and building an Atmanirbhar Bharat.“Imagine, 100 years have passed, but in 1930, Gandhi left us with this message, and today, so many years later, I too have to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure? Don't listen to me; at least you could have to listen to Gandhi! (Meri mat mano, par Gandhi kih toh mano bhai). He too spoke of Swadeshi before leaving; he too spoke of Atmanirbhar Bharat (Self-Reliant India). And now you have turned 100 years old, yet things remain right where they were . .. Spread my message too to every home!” he said.PM Modi also cautioned businesses against taking India's large domestic market for granted, urging them to focus on product quality and ensure their offerings meet international standards.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor backs PM Modi on corporates, not on corruption. PM Modi criticised industry leaders for not translating the benefits of corporate tax cuts into higher employee salaries or additional jobs. PM urged industry to openly suggest reforms and assured them that the government was willing to consider their proposals.

NEW DELHI: Authorities will conduct nationwide checks of packaged drinking water brands in the wake of safety findings against Bisleri, a government source told Reuters.The move comes after a row between the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) and Bisleri International. A sample of the company's packaged drinking water was initially declared unsafe, prompting the regulator to sanction prosecution against it.Subsequent testing found Bisleri's samples compliant with food safety regulations, government sources informed Reuters. The regulator had also recalled batches of the company's packaged water that were found unsafe.Bisleri said the matter related to a batch produced at its Goa facility in September 2025. It said five of the six samples collected by FSSAI met applicable standards, while the sixth recorded bromate levels above the prescribed limit.The company appealed against the findings, and the sample was sent to a referral laboratory. Bisleri said the laboratory found bromate within the prescribed limit but separately flagged polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).Bisleri said an independent test of the same sample at an FSSAI-approved laboratory also found bromate within the prescribed limit. It said it submitted the results to the regulator in February 2026 and received no further communication, leading it to believe the matter had been closed.The company said it had not received the reported notice by email or in hard copy. It added that drinking water safety remained a priority and that it would cooperate with FSSAI.FSSAI had earlier said the sample was declared unsafe after failing to meet prescribed bromate limits. The referral laboratory also declared it unsafe after detecting PAHs, the regulator said.The action comes as FSSAI intensifies its enforcement drive against food businesses and e-commerce companies.
Article Summary: India to conduct nationwide packaged water checks after Bisleri sample controversy. A sample of the company's packaged drinking water was initially declared unsafe, prompting the regulator to sanction prosecution against it. The move comes after a row between the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) and Bislera International.

NEW DELHI: Foreign minister S Jaishankar called on Nepal PM Balendra Shah, who arrived in India on Sunday for what is his first bilateral visit abroad. PM Modi will host Shah for their first in-person meeting on Monday that will be followed by an exchange of "forward-looking" agreements spanning key areas of cooperation: infrastructure, technology, connectivity, development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, climate change and disaster resilience."India cherishes the special friendship with Nepal. Look forward to his engagements with PM @narendramodi tomorrow," said Jaishankar in a post on X after the meeting. Official sources said that the leaders will virtually inaugurate several completed initiatives, apart from joining foundation stone-laying ceremonies for some new projects. Shah is also expected to reiterate Nepal's request for two-way low-altitude air entry corridors through Indian airspace near western border entry points.Securing direct air routes is essential for Nepal to attract international airlines and make its new Bhairahawa airport commercially viable. “This visit comes at an opportune moment when there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of both countries in terms of economic growth, social development, expansion of infrastructure, adoption of technology and addressing issues like natural disasters and climate change,” said a source, adding that the leaders will look to provide political direction that will shape the roadmap for bilateral cooperation for many years to come.The two sides have finalised a joint vision for bilateral relations that is expected to be released after the meeting. Nepal is also seeking an economic package worth $2 billion from India. While Shah may raise the boundary issue, it’s unlikely to be a sticking point in the meeting.India sees its ties with Nepal as unique and comprehensive, characterised by mutual trust, open borders, shared traditions and close people-to-people ties. Govt sources highlighted how India is Nepal’s largest trade, transit and investment partner. Nepal enjoys duty-free access to the Indian market and India is also Nepal’s biggest export destination and receives about 80% of Nepal’s goods exports, they said.The visit is expected to build upon the goodwill generated in Nepal by India’s assistance to the country after the devastating floods earlier this year. India provided about 140 tonnes of emergency supplies and extended technical assistance in tunnel rescue and forensic activities following the flash flood.India and Nepal are exploring the development of new pipelines and terminals to further enhance energy connectivity. Both sides are also discussing new possibilities, such as the RaxaulKathmandu railway link, which could open new avenues for cross-border passenger and freight connectivity

Article Title: COP31 ends without climate pact as countries fail to reach consensus over fossil fuel omission and empty finance promises
Article Text:
COP31 failed to reach consensus on the proposed Antalya Pact, COP31 President Murat Kurum said

World staring at climate crisis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Countries on Sunday failed to reach an agreement at the 31st session of the UN climate conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey as there was no consensus over the cover decision (overarching political and binding outcome) -- a first such instance since 2009 despite stretching into overtime longer than ever before beyond its schedule time to conclude on Friday -- with some countries and groups including EU, Norway and Panama out-rightly objecting to the final deal for not even mentioning a call to transition away from fossil fuels in the text whereas others criticising it for empty climate finance promise. Incidentally, both Turkey and Australia - twin presidencies of this round of climate conference - are fossil fuel producing nations.India while intervening on behalf of the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) expressed the group's concerns flagging the "dilution of the historical responsibility and obligations of developed countries" in the text but stopped short of its outright rejection noting that they are "willing to move forward, and continue to engage" for the sake of multilateralism."Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, are willing to move forward, and continue to engage. A constructive approach going forward would be to respect the work we have done and move forward. We are committed to multilateralism and the principles of consensus and we invite our partners to join us as well," said India's key negotiator, Amandeep Garg, additional secretary in the environment ministry, in his intervention.China during the final plenary agreed to what India maintained and even said this in as many words but chose to accept the version of the final text to keep things moving forward."I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome. I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," said the UN secretary-general, Antonio Guterres.The only other time a COP collapsed before 2009 (COP15 in Copenhagen) was COP6 in the Hague in 2000. The COP15 is, however, considered the biggest disappointment in the history of climate negotiations due to its much wider goal where a legally binding climate agreement could not be reached despite much political hype and preparations ahead of it.Though the COP31 accepted a few decisions and even retained an ambitious '35 by 35' electrification goal as a key takeaway, most of the developing countries expressed strong dissatisfaction over the unresolved amount for the adaptation finance and a move of deploying carbon capture, utilization and storage (CCUS) by 2035 that called for wider deployment of CO2 removal technologies. Many countries argued that the CCUS move raises serious questions about the direction of global mitigation efforts.Under the '35 by 35' target, electricity would supply 35% of global final energy consumption by 2035. At present, the share of electricity in global energy consumption is 23%. The move recognizes the need for stronger grids, storage, system flexibility and better energy access, but the text mentions no specific financial commitments for this aspiration. It also ignored the firm commitment of renewable-powered electrification.In India, electricity currently makes up roughly 22% of the country’s total final energy consumption, with the remainder dominated by oil, coal and natural gas. The country has voluntarily moved quite fast on increasing its renewable footprints, way above many developing countries.COP31 even failed to bridge the overall adaptation finance gap, leaving many developing countries extremely disappointed. India, on behalf of the LMDC, too flagged it in the plenary."... our partners have refused to engage on the issue of climate finance across different negotiating rooms. In fact, we were told that despite the increasing needs of developing countries due to a problem that we have not caused, we should not expect our developed country partners to even engage on the issue of climate finance, since it was 'dead in the water'," Garg told the plenary.Many experts consider COP31 a big political failure as it happened amid wars, geopolitical tensions, economic uncertainty and mounting climate risks. Countries across the globe are facing growing pressures over energy security, industrial competitiveness and public finances, while developing nations struggle with rising adaptation costs and increasingly severe climate impacts. They also flagged that the EU failed miserably to take climate leadership in the absence of the USA which under President Donald Trump stepped out from the Paris Agreement.Developed countries, mainly the EU nations, the UK and Japan resisted measurable commitments to fund climate action while the major fossil fuel producing nations including Saudi Arabia and Russia opposed stronger language on transitioning away from oil, gas and coal. The result was a text that found space for an electrification goal and CCUS but not for strong anti-fossil fuel commitments or public finance needed by developing nations.“The COP 31 outcome reflects an abject lack of political ambition and accountability. Despite negotiations extending till Sunday, countries failed to agree on a meaningful commitment to transition away from fossil fuels or to talk about climate security. There is over emphasis on the unknown devil of CCUS which presents a grave concern of untested technology, and serious implications to forest and food security in many parts of the world," said Aarti Khosla, director, Climate Trends.Harjeet Singh, founding director of the Satat Sampada Climate Foundation, said the COP31 failed the people it was meant to protect. "Rich countries refused to put money on the table to help communities prepare for and recover from climate disasters, and handed polluters a free pass instead. No deal is better than a deal that locks in failure. But this cannot become an excuse for more delay: the money and the plan must now come," he said.
Article Summary: There was no consensus over the cover decision (overarching political and binding outcome) for the first time since 2009. Some countries and groups including EU, Norway and Panama out-rightly objected to the final deal for not even mentioning a call to transition away from fossil fuels in the text.

NEW DELHI: India has retained its position among Asia's top three most powerful countries, with its overall power score rising to 40.5 points in 2026, according to a report by the Lowy Institute.The 2026 Asia Power Index also highlights an increasingly contested regional balance, with the gap between the United States and China narrowing largely due to Washington's missteps rather than Beijing's advances. Prime Minister Narendra Modi's regional leadership assessment also improved, with the report placing him second among Asia's regional leaders.Here are the top key findings:The United States and China continue to dominate Asia's power rankings, but the gap between them has narrowed to its lowest level since the index was launched in 2018. The US leads with 78.9 points, followed by China at 73.6 — a difference of just 5.3 points. The gap in military capability has also narrowed to its smallest recorded level.India ranks third with 40.5 points, followed by Japan with 38.6 points, placing both among Asia's major powers.The gap between India's and China's overall power narrowed to its lowest level since the Asia Power Index was first published in 2018, although China's power remains 80% higher than India's.Prime Minister Narendra Modi was also ranked Asia's second-most effective regional leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping, improving three places.However, perceptions of his global leadership and strategic ambition declined, with India's muted response to the sinking of an Iranian naval vessel by a US submarine during the Gulf conflict cited as an example of its lower diplomatic profile.India's Diplomatic Influence, however, remained its strongest measure at 70.3 points, slipping only marginally in a year when most countries faltered.India's economic capability score dipped slightly to 26.4 points, with a weakening rupee, changes in the International Monetary Fund's methodology and a nearly $20 billion drop in outbound investment weighing on its relative GDP standing.The United States recorded its steepest-ever decline in diplomatic influence in 2026, with the Trump administration's unilateral foreign policy, trade tariffs and war with Iran eroding its standing across Asia. Washington's strained ties with international institutions, along with President Donald Trump's remarks on arms sales to Taiwan and military exercises with South Korea, further weakened regional confidence in US leadership.The US Diplomatic Influence score fell by six points to 76.7, marking the fourth consecutive year of decline and the biggest single-year drop in the measure since the Asia Power Index was launched in 2018.The 2026 Asia Power Index evaluates 27 countries and territories across 131 indicators covering eight measures of power, including economic and military capability, resilience, diplomatic influence and economic relationships.
Article Summary: India ranks third with 40.5 points, followed by Japan with 38.6 points. The gap between India's and China's overall power narrowed to its lowest level since the Asia Power Index was first published in 2018. Prime Minister Narendra Modi was also ranked Asia's second-most effective regional leader, behind Chinese President Xi Jinping, improving three places.

AHMEDABAD: The anti-immigration crackdown in US has swept 1,389 unaccompanied Indian children into custody since America’s FY23. These children have not been repatriated.However, the unyielding drive against immigrants has reduced the number of unaccompanied Indian children found in US: 730 in FY23, 517 in FY24, 91 in FY25, 51 in FY26, and two in Oct 2026, the first month of US FY27.The data is from US Customs and Border Protection (USCBP).The decline mirrors the trend for unaccompanied children of all nationalities. US authorities recorded 1.1 lakh unaccompanied children in FY24, 29,584 in FY25, and 9,190 in FY26. In Oct 2026, 722 children were found unaccompanied.People familiar with immigration networks in US said the decline could partly be linked to stricter enforcement and faster deportations. Earlier, minors were allegedly used as ‘green card bringers’ to help parents or relatives strengthen their chances of obtaining legal status.This practice is reportedly becoming less common as authorities swiftly deport those caught.A businessman from Kadi, who was deported from US in 2012, said his 17-year-old son, who has been living in Texas since he was 12, is now afraid to attend his asylum hearings.“He thinks he will be caught and deported to India. He has been secretly working at a gas station and living with members of a religious sect,” the businessman said.The trend comes even as Indians continue to feature among the top nationalities attempting illegal entry into US. In FY26, US authorities recorded 30,528 encounters with Indian nationals, placing India third among 21 countries, behind Mexico and Canada.
Article Summary: The number of Indian minors travelling without parents or guardians were 730 in FY23, 517 in FY24, 91 in FY25 and 51 in FY26. In Oct 2026, 722 children were found unaccompanied. The decline mirrors the trend for unaccompanied children of all nationalities.

NEW DELHI: In a big milestone for the country’s nuclear sector, Kaiga Generating Station Unit-1 (KGS-1) in Karnataka successfully attained criticality early Sunday for the second time, giving a new lease of life to the nuclear power unit that had been taken offline for life-extension work after 25 years of operation. The disclosure was made on Sunday by Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), the PSU that designs, builds, commissions and operates nuclear power plants across India.A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core.KGS-1 had reached first criticality on Sept 26, 2000, and had supplied 37,670 million units before it was shut down for refurbishment activities in April last year. The same unit had set a world record for 962 days of continuous operation on Dec 31, 2018, operating at a 99.3% plant load factor, surpassing the previous global record of 940 days held by Heysham II (Unit 8/Reactor 2) in the UK.“The accomplishing this in just 600 days following its shutdown for major refurbishment activities of EMCCR (en-masse coolant channel replacement) and EMFR (en-masse feeder replacement) on April 1, 2025, KGS-1 has set a new fleet-wide benchmark as the first NPCIL reactor to reach criticality in such a short span,” NPCIL said on X on Sunday.It said, “This remarkable success stands as a reflection of extraordinary dedication, technical excellence, and unified teamwork. ”Kaiga generating station has four operational nuclear units totalling 880 MW and two additional units (5 and 6) under construction, adding 1,400 MW and bringing the total planned capacity to 2,280 MW across six units.Kaiga Units-5 & 6 are state-of-the-art, indigenous 700 MW pressurized heavy-water reactors (PHWRs), which incorporate advanced safety features and are among the safest in the world. Three such PHWRs — KAPS-3&4 and RAPP-7 — are successfully operating in the states of Gujarat and Rajasthan respectively. The components and equipment for the project are supplied by domestic industry partners and works are being executed by Indian contractors, aligning with the Atmanirbhar initiatives of the Modi govt.Just days before, in another development, Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) granted permission for the first approach to criticality of Rajasthan atomic power project unit-8 (RAPP-8) at Rawatbhata, following satisfactory completion of safety reviews.
Article Summary: Kaiga Generating Station Unit-1 (KGS-1) in Karnataka successfully attained criticality early Sunday for the second time. A unit attaining criticality means it has reached a self-sustaining, controlled nuclear fission chain reaction inside its reactor core.

NEW DELHI: Easing rules to make naval jobs more attractive, the Indian Navy has allowed Agniveers who opt for a two-year extension after the initial four-year service to get married. The policy relaxation comes just as the first batch of Naval Agniveers — recruited in late 2022 — completes its initial four-year stint this month. The Union Cabinet recently approved a two-year extended service period for Agniveers, officially called ‘Second Tour of Duty’.“Those Agniveers who have completed their four-year initial service period and have opted for the two-year extension will be allowed to marry, though only after completion of their mandatory initial training on joining. The training will be professional and trade specific,” a defence source told TOI. After completing their training, Agniveers can take the entitled leave for marriage purposes, the source said.The marriage provision is currently not available for Naval Agniveers (ages 17.5 to 21) during the initial four-year service period under the Agnipath scheme. “Navy has made the decision on marriage provision and orders have been issued,” the source said. After the Navy, Indian Army and Indian Air Force could follow suit by allowing Agniveers to marry as per their own specifications.On Nov 4, Chief of Defence Staff General N S Raja Subramani announced the ‘Second Tour of Duty’ provision under the Agnipath scheme, increasing Agniveers’ service duty period from four years to six with increased remuneration. Govt has also decided to create a pathway for “all Agniveers to be enrolled as regular soldiers (permanent job)” if they are willing to continue and meet selection criteria. NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) on Sunday sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd after a sample of its packaged drinking water was found unsafe.In a social media post, the food safety regulator said a sample of "Packaged Drinking Water (other than Mineral Water)" collected from Bisleri's premises was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards."The sample was found non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under the FSS Act, 2006," FSSAI said.The company subsequently appealed against the findings, following which the sample was sent to a referral food laboratory for further analysis.The laboratory also declared it "unsafe" after detecting polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the regulator said.Based on the laboratory findings, FSSAI concluded that the company had violated provisions relating to unsafe food under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. It has, therefore, sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd under the law.Apart from Bisleri, the regulator also sanctioned prosecution against several other companies, including Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd, Tit-Bit Foods India Pvt Ltd, Mimansa Industries and Asha Confectionery.FSSAI also suspended the licences of Urmi Lifesciences LLP and Gaur Ayurvedic Store for non-compliance with food safety rules and regulations, news agency PTI reported.The latest action comes amid an intensified enforcement drive by FSSAI against food business operators (FBOs) and e-commerce companies during the current calendar year. The regulator has also stepped up scrutiny of energy drink and alcoholic beverage manufacturers.One of its recent regulatory disputes involves the classification of Red Bull as an "energy drink". In June, FSSAI moved against the use of the label, raising concerns that the high added-sugar content of certain beverages could mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption.Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer challenged the regulator's order in the Delhi high court, arguing that the restrictions were imposed without giving them prior notice.Red Bull subsequently secured an interim court injunction allowing it to continue using the "energy drink" label. Its competitors, however, were directed to stop using the classification after exhausting their existing stocks.FSSAI has challenged the relief granted to Red Bull, arguing that it gives the company "an undue commercial advantage" over its rivals. The matter is scheduled to be heard in January.
Article Summary: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India sanctions prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd. The regulator says a sample of its packaged drinking water was found unsafe. NEW DELHI: India and Nepal on Monday signed eight agreements to expand cooperation in sectors including space technology, security, healthcare, agriculture and sustainable urban development, following talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.The two leaders also virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur in Nepal, and jointly inaugurated several development projects during Balen Shah’s two-day state visit to India.At a joint press conference after the talks, Modi said the two countries had taken several important decisions to strengthen bilateral relations.“I am very pleased to welcome Balendra Shah ji to India on his first bilateral visit after becoming the Prime Minister of Nepal. A few months ago, when he addressed the United Nations as the world’s youngest Prime Minister, we got a clear glimpse of his vision. Over the past few hours of our discussions, I have sensed his clear vision and commitment towards Nepal’s future and India-Nepal relations. The historic mandate given to him by the people of Nepal this year reflects the aspirations and hopes of the country’s younger generation. India has always been a partner in the development journey of a strong and prosperous Nepal.In this spirit, today we have taken several important decisions to take our relations to new heights,” PM Modi said.The prime minister also announced a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees (approximately Rs 15,000 crore) to support Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development, particularly in the wake of the devastating floods in August.“We express our deep condolences for the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods in Nepal in August. Today, we announce a development cooperation package of 24,000 crore Nepali rupees to give fresh impetus to Nepal’s reconstruction and long-term development. Our commitment will be to help affected families get their lives back on track, create new opportunities, and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” he said.PM Modi also highlighted the shared religious and cultural ties between the two countries, referring to the launch of the train service connecting Ayodhya and Janakpur.“Lord Ram and Mata Sita are symbols of our shared civilisation and faith. In 2018, on the sacred land of Janakpur, I had said that our pilgrimage sites are incomplete without Nepal, and our Lord Ram is incomplete without Nepal. In 2024, the consecration ceremony of Ram Lalla took place in Ayodhya. This historic occasion gave renewed strength to our shared faith…With the launch of the Sarayu-Kamala Express train service today, we are giving a new dimension to this sacred bond,” he said.He said India had maintained supplies of fuel and other essential goods to Nepal despite serious challenges related to oil supplies this year, and expressed confidence in the future of bilateral ties.“We will together write a golden chapter of India-Nepal relations,” PM Modi said.The Saryu-Kamala Express will connect Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal, covering around 604 km in approximately 19 hours. The regular service will operate once a week in each direction from November 28, enabling pilgrims to travel between the two religious destinations without changing trains.The inaugural run on Monday operated as a special train (No. 04295), departing from Ayodhya Dham at 12.30 pm.The eight MoUs exchanged after the delegation-level talks cover satellite communication, policing, forensic sciences, civil service training, healthcare, traditional medicine, sustainable urban development, and livestock and fisheries development.In the space and communication sector, the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Nepal’s Ministry of Information and Communication signed an MoU to establish a Satellite Communication (SATCOM) Network for the utilisation of the South Asia Satellite.Two agreements aim to strengthen cooperation in policing and forensic sciences. One provides for academic and research collaboration between the National Forensic Sciences University in Gandhinagar, Gujarat, and the Crime Investigation Department of Nepal Police. The other was signed between India’s Rashtriya Raksha University and Nepal’s National Police Academy.For capacity building in public administration, the National Centre for Good Governance, under India’s Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, signed an MoU with Nepal’s Administrative Staff College under the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration. The agreement provides for training programmes for Nepalese civil servants.In healthcare, India’s Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and Nepal’s Ministry of Health and Food Safety signed an MoU on cooperation in health and medicine. The two sides also signed a government-to-government agreement on cooperation in Ayurveda and other traditional systems of medicine.The remaining two agreements provide for technical cooperation in sustainable urban development and collaboration in livestock and fisheries development.At the joint press conference, Balen Shah described India-Nepal relations as being founded on mutual respect, trust and goodwill.“Ties between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as oceans,” he said.He expressed confidence that the agreements and initiatives announced during the visit would take bilateral relations to a new level, while stressing the need for cooperation on climate change.“I am confident that these historic milestones will elevate Nepal-India relations to new heights. The need of the hour is to build on the strong foundation of this enduring relationship and lay solid pillars for the future. Our Himalayas, the sources of clean water, sustain millions across this region. The pristine rivers flowing from the Himalayas into the Ganga remind us of our future and destiny, underscoring the need to address the challenges of climate change through collective action. Nepal and India have been bound by historical, cultural and civilisational ties since the sacred era of Lord Ram and Mata Janaki,” Balen Shah said.Balen Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for a two-day state visit, his first to India since assuming office in March 2026.On Monday, PM Modi received him at Hyderabad House for the bilateral talks. Before the meeting, Shah was accorded a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan and paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at the Raj Ghat memorial.Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in a post on X that the leaders would discuss various aspects of bilateral relations and explore new avenues to deepen cooperation.Jaiswal described the ceremonial welcome as reflecting “the special warmth and enduring friendship between India and Nepal” and Shah’s visit to Raj Ghat as “A tribute to the timeless legacy of Mahatma!”
Article Summary: India and Nepal signed eight agreements to expand cooperation in sectors including space technology, security, healthcare, agriculture and sustainable urban development. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah virtually flagged off the Saryu-Kamala Express, connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur in Nepal.

Article Title: The decade India turned the tide on poverty
Article Text:
Nirmala Sitharaman

Targeted, focused and tailored

Health and dignity begin at home

From a bank account to an enterprise

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The sankalp for Viksit Bharat

(The writer is Union minister for finance & corporate affairs)

A year ago, during my visit to Kiphire, an aspirational district in the remote hills of Nagaland, I interacted with tribal women from local self-help groups. Among them was Esther, a Lakhpati Didi, who proudly spoke of her millet-based products reaching customers online, far beyond Nagaland.What stayed with me was their confidence in a better future. I encouraged them to dream bigger and become Crorepati Didis. Their stories reflected a transformation reaching India's remotest corners, where geographical and economic challenges have long constrained opportunities, yet aspirations for a better tomorrow are growing.When World Bank released its Poverty & Equity Brief on India last month, my interaction in Kiphire came back to me. The report showed that nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, while extreme poverty has been almost eradicated. These figures captured the transformation I had witnessed firsthand.It was not always so. For over six decades after Independence, eradicating mass poverty remained an unfulfilled promise. Even in the early 2010s, India was portrayed abroad as a home of enduring destitution, lagging in sanitation, nutrition, clean cooking fuel and banking.The prevailing prescription was simply to put money into the hands of the poor, and poverty would take care of itself.The last decade has overturned that belief. Under PM Narendra Modi's leadership, India has witnessed a fundamental shift from temporary relief to removing the barriers that perpetuate poverty. Guided by Antyodaya, the welfare of the last person in the line, our govt chose the harder path of addressing deprivations, ensuring development reached those who needed it most.Garibi is not merely a shortage of income or wages. A household without a secure roof, safe water, sanitation or healthcare remains vulnerable even when its income rises. One illness can wipe out savings and push a family back into poverty. Our govt, therefore, made every intervention targeted at those who needed it, focused on measurable outc-omes and tailored to the deprivation it was meant to remove.There was no magic wand. Each scheme required careful identification of beneficiaries, effective delivery and follow-up until the last household was reached. PM Modi has personally monitored implementation, intervened at critical junctures to resolve bottlenecks, ensured follow-ups and encouraged the use of technology to track delivery.A family cannot climb out of poverty while illness and the daily burden of fetching water keep pulling it back. Under Swachh Bharat, access to household toilets has improved sanitation and helped avert an estimated 60,000-70,000 infant deaths a year. Jal Jeevan Mission has expanded rural tap-water connections from about 3 crore households in 2019 to nearly 16 crore. Ujjwala Yojana has enabled cleaner, smokeless kitchens, while PM Awas Yojana has provided the security and dignity of pucca homes. Ayushman Bharat has strengthened financial protection against medical expenses.Protection keeps families from slipping back into poverty; to rise further, they need opportunities to earn. For crores of people, that journey began with a bank account. Over 59 crore Jan Dhan accounts enable benefits to reach recipients directly, without middlemen. Two months ago, during an interaction with Mudra beneficiaries, I met Sushmita Gharai from West Bengal. She lost her father during the pandemic, and her family's printing business collapsed. A collateral-free Mudra loan helped her restart the press. Today, she employs eight people, twice her initial workforce, and plans to expand into digital printing. What stayed with me was her determination to rebuild and grow.Women have led this transformation. Ten crore rural women participate in SHGs that, through the DAY-NRLM and other programmes, have become platforms for savings, skills, credit and entrepreneurship. Over 3.7 crore women have become Lakhpati Didis, with some going further to become Crorepati Didis.For generations, poverty was treated as something India could manage but never end. What appeared unimaginable a decade ago has now been achieved through years of steady work.Yet, this is no time to rest; the road to Viksit Bharat by 2047 brings its own challenges. Govt is building closer links between academia and industry through employment-linked incentives, internships and apprenticeships, while investment in infrastructure is connecting the country as never before.With the resolve of 140 crore Indians, Viksit Bharat by 2047 is within our reach, and we together will get there.
Article Summary: Nirmala Sitharaman: Nearly 50 crore Indians had moved out of poverty between 2011 and 2023. The World Bank released its Poverty & Equity Brief on India last month. Under PM Narendra Modi's leadership, India has witnessed a shift from temporary relief to removing barriers that perpetuate poverty.

India held bilateral talks with Iran on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum to explore avenues for cultural cooperation, with Tehran proposing the establishment of a joint network to preserve manuscripts and shared civilisational heritage.Union culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal confirmed the bilateral engagement on Sunday, saying the two countries remained in regular touch on areas of potential cultural exchange. He added that several ideas were discussed during the meeting, though no specific project had been finalised."There was a bilateral meeting with Iran. And India is in constant touch with Iran, and on areas in which there can be any cultural exchange, we are always in discussion. And discussions took place during the Summit too," Aggarwal told reporters at the historic Purana Quila, the venue of the three-day forum."Ideas have been thrown, though no such project has been concretised yet. But the discussions and engagements are on," he added.The Iranian Embassy in India, in a post on X on Sunday, said Tehran had proposed setting up an "SCO Joint Network for Written Heritage and Civilisational Memory" at the forum.Dr Faridoddin Faridasr, Cultural Counsellor of the Islamic Republic of Iran in India, addressed the First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi, highlighting the importance of shared civilisational heritage as a foundation for cultural cooperation and mutual understanding among SCO member states, the embassy said.In his remarks, Faridasr emphasised the historical role of the Persian language as a language of science, literature, administration and cultural exchange across Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring regions, describing it as an important part of the shared cultural and historical heritage of the region.He also highlighted the work of the Noor International Microfilm Centre, affiliated with the Iranian Embassy in New Delhi, as an example of cultural cooperation between the two countries.Since 1990, the centre has collaborated with 72 academic and cultural institutions in India, resulting in the digitisation of "more than 150,000 Persian and Arabic manuscripts," the restoration and preservation of over three million pages of historical documents, and the preparation of nearly 300 catalogues, the embassy said.Faridasr also referred to ongoing joint projects with cultural institutions in Telangana and Hyderabad for the digitisation, restoration and preservation of historical Persian documents and manuscripts.Outlining the proposed SCO network as a practical initiative to strengthen regional cultural cooperation, the embassy said it would focus on preserving and digitising manuscripts and historical documents, exchanging technical expertise and providing training in manuscript restoration. It would also promote shared linguistic and literary heritage through joint research, publications and exhibitions.Faridasr reaffirmed Iran's "readiness to share its experience and technical expertise with other SCO member states", stressing that the preservation of shared civilisational heritage provided an opportunity to strengthen mutual trust, cultural understanding and cooperation across the region.Meanwhile, Aggarwal said no formal bilateral meeting took place between India and Pakistan on the sidelines of the forum, although members of the two sides interacted during banquets and conference sessions."There were no formal bilateral talks between the two sides," he said, responding to a question on whether any formal engagement had taken place between the two countries.He added that there were other "informal discussions" during the course of the event, including interactions with ministers and heads of delegations from participating countries."In general, there were also meetings between ministers and heads of delegations, as the aim of this (multilateral) forum is to exchange views, so there were many meetings, and a lot of things were discussed," the culture secretary said.Pakistan's Federal Minister Musadik Masood Malik, who attended the three-day forum, said he was in India to discuss regional issues and cultural ties in the context of the SCO, and not the Indus Waters Treaty."When you will call me for talk on Indus (Water Treaty), that time, we will surely talk on Indus (treaty). This time, you have not called me here for (talks on) the Indus treaty; this time you have called me to talk...," Malik told reporters."You have called me this time to talk about the issue in the context of the SCO forum, the regional issues, its relationship with culture, for which I am here," he said.The three-day forum, held from November 20 to 22, was organised by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs. It was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on November 20 and saw the participation of delegates from various SCO member countries, including Iran and Pakistan, as well as other countries.
Article Summary: India, Iran hold talks on cultural cooperation on sidelines of SCO forum. Tehran proposes the establishment of a joint network to preserve manuscripts and shared civilisational heritage. No formal bilateral meeting took place between India and Pakistan on the sidelines of the forum.

Article Title: SCO Civilisational Dialogue at Purana Qila concludes with 'Indraprastha Communique' affirming to respect every civilisation as an 'equal voice'
Article Text:
SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum

NEW DELHI: The first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum hosted by India at the historic Purana Qila concluded on Sunday with the “Indraprastha Communique” -- an outcome document with affirmations ranging from protecting heritage from threats and exploring joint nominations for UNESCO heritage tag to constructively using Artificial Intelligence and creating a digital repository of manuscripts and records of cultural histories.The communique affirmed respect for every civilisation as an “equal voice”, and acknowledged its identity and contribution to humanity. Reading out the communique at the closing session of the meet on Sunday evening, culture secretary Vivek Aggarwal said that India has proposed that the SCO Civilisational Dialogue be held once every two years at a place to be decided by the SCO member states.The three-day meet inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday saw the participation of 116 delegates from 22 countries, including Pakistan’s federal minister Musadik Malik. PM Modi had proposed the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the 25th SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025 and the idea was welcomed and endorsed subsequently enabling India to host the first Forum in Delhi from Nov 20 to 22.The venue, Purana Qila, took centre stage at the event as India showcased the site’s multi-layered history and its identity as the ancient city of Indraprastha mentioned in the epic ‘Mahabharata’.The name of the communique reaffirmed that message, which was reiterated by India through the layers of excavations and exhibits displayed at Purana Qila during the meet, presenting thousands of years of history.The communique called for celebrating “diversity as a strength” and recognised culture as a “vital bridge for friendship, good neighbourliness among nations”.The outcome document also highlighted the need to evolve an SCO mechanism for collaborative projects and exhibitions and a platform for collaboration between cultural institutions of SCO countries. To protect heritage from various kinds of threats, it called for exploring the creation of a platform for resilience against climatic tragedies.It further called for honouring spiritual and philosophical traditions, and places of learning and pilgrimage, and encouraging respectful dialogue with due regard for diversity of beliefs and practices.Asked if any formal bilateral talks were held between India and Pakistan on the sidelines of the event, Aggarwal answered in the negative, but said that just as with other member countries, the Indian side had interactions with Pakistan’s representative during the course of the event.On Sunday evening, Musadik visited the Mahabharata Pavillion displaying the rare 18th century Mahabharata scroll. He called it “very impressive”, appreciated its artistic and religious value, and lauded the commitment of the artist for the delicate and intricate work on the scroll.He reiterated the affirmation made in the Indraprastha Communique of working with SCO members to create a digital repository of manuscripts from the region and said that Pakistan would be keen to explore showcasing knowledge about many artefacts, including those excavated from Mohenjo-Daro, once a framework is developed for the same.He expressed optimism that cross-border visits and regional relationships would improve ahead of Pakistan’s hosting the next SCO Council of Heads of State summit in Islamabad in August 2027.The first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in India was organised jointly by the ministry of culture, and the ministry of external affairs with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) serving as the knowledge partner.On Saturday, the thematic session "Civilisational and Cultural Expressions" saw ministers and representatives of participating countries present their perspectives on their cultural traditions, historical experiences and areas of common interest. The exchanges brought into focus the importance of safeguarding tangible and intangible heritage, strengthening institutional linkages, encouraging interaction among scholars and artists, and advancing joint research and documentation.A dedicated session organised by the Archaeological Survey of India, titled "A Shared Cultural Canvas - Artistic and Architectural Exchanges Among SCO Nations", examined the many historical encounters that have shaped the region's artistic and architectural landscape. According to details shared by culture ministry and IGNCA discussions traversed prehistoric and Bronze Age linkages, Buddhist art and architecture, Silk Route exchanges, Indo-Persian influences and maritime connections, while also considering collaborative approaches to heritage conservation and digital documentation.On Sunday deliberations centred on two themes: "Language, Literature, Script and Manuscript Traditions" and "Monastic Trails - Religious and Philosophical Traditions". The first session explored approaches to preserving languages, scripts, manuscripts and literary heritage, as well as the transmission of knowledge across generations and geographical boundaries. The second examined the journeys of faith and philosophy and the historical relationships linking religious institutions, centres of learning and communities across the SCO region.
Article Summary: India hosted the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum. The three-day meet was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday. 116 delegates from 22 countries, including Pakistan’s federal minister Musadik Malik, attended.

Article Title: Absence of COP31 cover decision does not pause climate action in India, says Bhupender Yadav
Article Text:
Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav in Antalya, Turkey for COP31

NEW DELHI: Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav , who led India's delegation at COP31 in Antalya, Turkiye, said that the absence of a cover decision does not pause climate action and the country continues to deliver at home and remains committed to consensus-based multilateralism on the road to COP32 (the next annual UN climate conference in Ethiopia in 2027). He also cited an example of India's growing renewable energy footprint, which has already taken the solar power capacity to more than 170 GW."India engaged constructively and tirelessly with the Presidencies and other Parties. While concerns remain over certain elements of the cover decision, we remain committed to dialogue and constructive engagement until the very end to build consensus," said Yadav while regretting that the consensus on the cover decision could not be reached.In the context of the Global South's concerns, the minister said, "Climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries."Noting that India engaged constructively till the very end, working with BASIC and LMDC partners for a balanced outcome rooted in equity, CBDR-RC, climate finance and adaptation at COP31, he said, "India's voice shaped the draft COP31 outcome: food security, livelihoods and cultural practices recognised in action on methane; Article 9.1 obligations of developed countries recalled; equity and CBDR-RC at the heart of implementation."India, for the like-minded developing countries, raised a fundamental question at COP-31: Why are we here, and how did we arrive at this climate crisis? Historical and continuing emissions have consumed a disproportionate share of the global carbon budget. Equity and climate justice must therefore remain at the heart of our collective response."
Article Summary: Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav led India's delegation at COP31 in Antalya, Turkiye. Yadav said that the absence of a cover decision does not pause climate action. He said India remains committed to consensus-based multilateralism on the road to COP32.

Article Title: Now, pilots’ body raise safety concerns for SpiceJet; seek urgent assessment of airline by DGCA
Article Text:
SpiceJet

NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has warned govt about SpiceJet’s severe financial stress’ “potential implications for aviation safety.” “Of particular is the impact of delayed and non-payment of salaries on pilots and other operational personnel. Financial insecurity can lead to anxiety, psychological stress, sleep disturbances and mental Fatigue, potentially affecting human performance and, consequently, flight safety,” FIP president Captain CS Randhawa has written to Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu.SpiceJet has not paid employees for months and has PF and TDS dues for a much longer period. Aviation authorities had till recently not intervened as the airline, which barely operates a handful of flights now, was leaving passengers stranded for many weeks now. While it sells tickets for its schedule without operating a vast majority of flights, the authorities did not intervene to protect consumer interest.In a much belated move, the DGCA only recently issued it a show cause notice. “SpiceJet crisis should serve as a wake-up call for the Indian Aviation industry. Financial sustainability of Airlines and aviation safety are intrinsically linked, and a proactive regulatory mechanism is essential to prevent financial distress from developing into an operational or safety crisis,” says the representation.FIP has expressed concern at the struggling-to-survive airline’s “financial distress, including accumulated liabilities; aircraft grounding; liquidity constraints; delayed salary payments; increasing operational costs and outstanding dues to various service providers.” It has asked minister Naidu to do an “urgent financial and operational safety assessment of SpiceJet by DGCA,” while calling for a more cost-friendly environment for airlines in India along with “introduction of a comprehensive financial early-warning mechanism for all scheduled airlines. ”The airline’s board had last Wednesday approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore “through one or more fundraising routes”. However, no prospective investor/s were named as the airline operates barely a handful of flights. Airline CMD Ajay Singh had said in a statement after the board meeting: “We believe this fundraise will provide an important opportunity to rebuild the airline, strengthen its operations and restore the brand.We are conscious of the challenges ahead, but we have a clear plan and are focused on putting the necessary building blocks in place. Our priority is to execute that plan with discipline and restore SpiceJet’s position as a strong and competitive airline.”
Article Summary: SpiceJet has not paid employees for months and has PF and TDS dues for a much longer period. Aviation authorities had till recently not intervened as the airline, which barely operates a handful of flights now, was leaving passengers stranded for many weeks now.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites
