NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Karnal woman books 2BHK flat in 2015, pays initial Rs 4.36 lakh but skips further instalments, consumer commission dismisses refund complaint, says developer not liable as over 90% work is complete
Article Text:
A homebuyer named Ankita Manocha lodged a complaint against Aegis Value Homes Ltd for alleged service deficiencies (AI-generated image used for representational purposes)





KARNAL: A homebuyer who booked a two-bedroom flat in a Karnal housing project in 2015 but failed to make any further payments beyond the initial Rs 4.36 lakh has suffered a setback, with the district consumer disputes redressal commission dismissing her complaint against the developer.The commission observed that the complainant had deposited Rs 4,36,263 but failed to make subsequent payments in accordance with the agreed instalment schedule. It held that, in the circumstances, the developer could not be held responsible for the alleged deficiency in service.The detailed order was passed on November 16, 2026, by a bench comprising commission president Jaswant Singh and members Neeru Agarwal and Sarvjeet Kaur. The case concerned Ankita Manocha versus Aegis Value Homes Ltd.The complainant had booked a two-bedroom flat in the developer's Ananda Phase-I affordable housing project in 2015. The project was proposed to be developed in Sector 32, near Noor Mahal Hotel in Karnal.She alleged that the company had assured buyers that the project would be completed and possession handed over within 48 months. She paid Rs 4,36,263 towards the apartment.In her complaint, Manocha alleged that despite making repeated visits to the project site, she found no significant progress in construction and development work. She also claimed that the company's officials failed to provide satisfactory responses when she approached them for updates.She subsequently sought a refund of the deposited amount and served a legal notice on the company dated October 5, 2021.However, as the money was not returned, she approached the consumer commission seeking a refund with 24% annual interest, Rs 25,000 as compensation for mental agony and harassment, and Rs 22,000 towards litigation expenses.Opposing the complaint, the company submitted that the basic sale price of the flat was Rs 17,45,053. Under the agreed payment plan, the buyer was required to clear the entire amount within 36 months of the issuance of the allotment letter.The developer maintained that it had issued payment demands and reminders to the complainant in 2015 and 2016. However, she did not deposit any further amount after making the initial payment of Rs 4.36 lakh.The company further submitted that more than 90% of the construction work had been completed and that the process of obtaining an Occupation Certificate (OC) from the concerned departments was underway.It also attributed the delay partly to the Covid-19 pandemic, which had disrupted construction activities and led to the migration of labourers. The company additionally cited delayed payments by the complainant and other allottees.After examining the documents and submissions made by both sides, the commission concluded that the complainant had failed to adhere to the agreed payment schedule.It noted that she had not deposited any further amount after the initial payment of Rs 4,36,263.The commission observed that the developer had completed more than 90% of the construction work despite the complainant's failure to comply with the payment schedule. It consequently held that no deficiency in service could be attributed to the developer.Finding no merit in the complaint, the commission dismissed it. It also ordered that there would be no order as to costs
Article Summary: Ankita Manocha lodged a complaint against Aegis Value Homes Ltd for alleged service deficiencies. She had booked a two-bedroom flat in the developer's Ananda Phase-I affordable housing project in 2015. The commission observed that the complainant had deposited Rs 4,36,263 but failed to make subsequent payments.

Article Title: Panchkula woman gets only Rs 18 of Rs 19 refund for unavailable chocolates in two grocery orders, Re 1 each diverted to rewards wallet, consumer commission flags orders company to pay Rs 7,500 payout
Article Text:
(AI image) A consumer commission in Panchkula directed a retail company to pay Rs 7,500 to Nishtha Raghav.

Two orders, two incomplete refunds

Why commission flagged a dark pattern





PANCHKULA: A consumer commission has directed a retail company to pay Rs 7,500 after finding that it diverted Re 1 from each of two grocery refunds into a digital rewards wallet instead of returning the entire amount to a customer's bank account.Flagging the practice as a potential ‘dark pattern’, the commission observed that such wallet credits could encourage consumers to revisit the platform and make further purchases to utilise their money.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Panchkula, allowed a complaint filed by 24-year-old Nishtha Raghav, holding the opposite parties jointly and severally liable for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The commission awarded her Rs 2,500 as lump-sum compensation and directed the opposite parties to deposit another Rs 5,000 as punitive damages with the Free Legal Aid State Commission, Haryana. The order was passed on October 28, 2026.According to the order, Raghav placed a grocery order worth Rs 319 on January 23, 2026, for herself and her brother. The order included a Munch Max Chocolate bar weighing 38.5g, which was subsequently found unavailable.She placed another order worth Rs 116 on January 25, which also included the same chocolate. The product was unavailable on this occasion too.On both occasions, the platform communicated that Rs 19 would be refunded to her original mode of payment. However, only Rs 18 from each transaction was credited to her bank account, while the remaining Re 1 was adjusted against her digital rewards wallet.Raghav alleged that she had neither consented to the adjustment nor been informed that part of the refund would be credited to the wallet instead of her bank account.She raised a written complaint through the shopping application on February 3, but her grievance was marked resolved without the relief sought. She subsequently sent a legal notice by email and speed post on February 14. The local store received it on February 16, while the retail company's registered office received it on February 17. However, the issue remained unresolved.The commission observed that a bank account and a rewards wallet were distinct modes of holding and utilising monetary value. A consumer could not be compelled to accept wallet credit instead of a refund to the original payment method, particularly when the company had represented that the money would be returned through that mode.It noted that the opposite parties had failed to produce any evidence establishing that Raghav had consented to the adjustment or accepted a disclosed refund policy permitting such a practice.In its order, the commission said diverting Re 1 from the refund into a restricted rewards wallet effectively retained part of the consumer's money within the digital rewards ecosystem. Such a credit could create an incentive for the consumer to return to the same platform and undertake another transaction to utilise the balance.The commission said the repeated practice, without the consumer's informed consent, raised concerns about manipulation of consumer choice and autonomy. Referring to the Central Consumer Protection Authority's Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, it observed that such practices could constitute unfair or deceptive trade practices.The order also noted that the opposite parties had appeared through a lawyer but failed to file their written statement despite being given several opportunities. Their defence was consequently struck off on June 26, 2026. However, the commission clarified that this did not automatically entitle the complainant to the relief sought and examined her affidavit and documentary evidence on their merits.Holding that the repeated diversion of refund amounts could not be treated as a mere inadvertent accounting error, the commission allowed the complaint and directed the opposite parties to comply with the order within 45 days of receiving its communication.
Article Summary: A consumer commission in Panchkula directed a retail company to pay Rs 7,500 to Nishtha Raghav. The commission awarded her Rs 2,500 as lump-sum compensation and directed the opposite parties to deposit another Rs 5,000 as punitive damages with the Free Legal Aid State Commission, Haryana.

Article Title: Raipur contractor's two excavators go missing after breakdown in 2023, Oriental Insurance disputes theft claim, state commission orders Rs 1.03 crore payout with 6% interest
Article Text:
Chhattisgarh state consumer disputes redressal commission partly allowed cross-appeals regarding a theft claim of excavators (AI-generated image used for representational purposes)





RAIPUR: Chhattisgarh state consumer disputes redressal commission in Raipur has partly allowed cross-appeals filed by The Oriental Insurance Company Limited and a contractor, modifying a district commission order in a theft claim involving two excavators.The bench of president justice Gautam Chourdiya and member Pramod Kumar Verma pronounced the order on November 4.The appeals challenged a May 20, 2026 ruling by the district consumer disputes redressal commission, additional bench, Raipur, which had directed the insurer to pay Rs 1,03,51,000 towards the insured declared value of an excavator (Rs 52,51,000) and another excavator (Rs 51,00,000), along with Rs 5 lakh for mental and physical distress and Rs 20,000 for litigation costs.According to the record, the contractor insured the two excavators from September 27, 2022 to September 26, 2023 and from November 9, 2022 to November 8, 2023 respectively under contractor’s plant and machinery floater policies.The contractor stated that the machines broke down on August 26, 2023, were parked about 800 metres off the road near Tandul village close to Rakhi police station in Raipur district, and were repaired with a mechanic.The operator left for his native village amid rain for two to three days, and when the contractor returned on August 28, 2023, the machines were missing.The contractor submitted a written request for a theft report at Rakhi police station on August 28, 2023 and complained to the senior superintendent of police in Raipur on August 29, 2023 after the police station did not register a report.Following a judicial magistrate’s order dated Oct 24, 2024, police registered an FIR and later filed a closure report.The insurance company contended that the complaint was time-barred, the machines were in transit rather than at the project site, the owner left them unguarded, and the absence of tyre or chain marks raised suspicion.The state commission rejected those objections, holding that the complaint filed on October 16, 2025 after a September 29, 2025 claim letter with the closure report was within limitation, the machines were parked near the site after a breakdown rather than in transit, and rain explained the absence of vehicle marks.Finding deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the insurer's part, the state commission deducted Rs 5,000 (Rs 2,500 per policy) as compulsory excess from Rs 1,03,51,000 to fix the payout at Rs 1,03,46,000.It ordered 6% annual interest from the date of filing the complaint until payment, ruled that ownership of the excavators would pass to the insurer upon payment if recovered.
Article Summary: Chhattisgarh state consumer disputes redressal commission partly allowed cross- appeals regarding a theft claim of excavators. The Oriental Insurance Company Limited and a contractor filed appeals. The appeals challenged a May 20, 2026 ruling by the district consumer disputes. commission, additional bench, Raipur.

Article Title: Petrol, diesel prices rose just 7% in India in four years versus 50-70% globally, says Hardeep Puri; but India’s oil and gas import bill has jumped 60% to $16 billion in October 2026 as Brent nearly d
Article Text:
Puri acknowledged that international conflicts and geopolitical uncertainty continued to pose challenges.

Government says oil price rise contained

India’s oil bill balloons

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the government reduce excise duty on fuel further? Yes, it will help consumers No, it may impact government revenue I'm indifferent to this issue 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

India has seen its petrol and diesel prices rise, but the government has said that the hike has much less compared to other major global economies.Oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said on Sunday that petrol and diesel prices in India had risen by just 7% over a four-year reference period, significantly less than the increase of 50-70% recorded in other parts of the world.He credited the relatively limited rise to three reductions in central excise duty and the role of oil marketing companies in absorbing losses instead of passing the entire burden on to consumers.Detailing the Centre’s efforts to keep fuel prices in check, Puri said excise duty had been cut on three occasions since November 2021. He maintained that, over the four-year period under consideration, fuel prices in India had actually declined.“India is a unique case globally….In fact, if you look at a four-year reference period, prices in India have actually decreased. Meanwhile, elsewhere in the world, petrol and diesel prices surged by 50–70%, whereas in India, they increased by only 7%,” Puri said.He said the divergence between domestic and international fuel price movements was the result of both the Centre’s three excise duty cuts and the actions of oil marketing companies.According to the minister, these companies took on substantial financial losses rather than transferring the full impact to customers.“This is because the central government reduced excise duty three times, and our oil marketing companies such as BPCL, IOCL, and HPCL acted as responsible corporate citizens. They absorbed significant losses and operated at a deficit,” he said.Puri acknowledged that international conflicts and geopolitical uncertainty continued to pose challenges. He expressed hope that tensions would eventually ease, paving the way for a decline in crude oil prices.“I am not speaking in the past tense, as if the matter is entirely behind us; we still face challenges. The war between Russia and Ukraine is ongoing, and there are also tensions involving Iran, the US, and Israel. We hope that these tensions subside and that the price of crude oil decreases,” he said.Meanwhile, India’s net expenditure on oil and gas imports climbed 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October, driven by a sharp rise in crude oil prices. Brent crude averaged $124.77 a barrel during the month, nearly twice its level a year earlier, according to data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), which functions under the oil ministry.The net import bill had stood at $10 billion in October 2025. Spending on crude oil imports alone increased to $19.5 billion from $10.4 billion a year earlier, although the volume of imports grew by just 11% to 23.3 million tonnes. Liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports accounted for $1.3 billion, while exports of petroleum products generated $6.3 billion.Brent crude had averaged $116.77 a barrel in September, compared with $64.75 in October 2025. The average price of India’s crude oil basket also rose sharply, reaching $119.91 a barrel in October against $65.08 in the corresponding month last year.For the April-October period, India’s net oil and gas import bill expanded to $97.7 billion from $70.3 billion a year earlier. Although crude oil import volumes increased by only 2.7%, the expenditure on these imports surged to $111 billion, compared with $72.3 billion in the year-ago period.Meanwhile, domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) consumption contracted by 12.3% in October and 15.1% during April-October. PPAC data showed that the number of active domestic LPG consumers declined to 32.6 crore as of November 1, from 33.4 crore on April 1.Direct imports of LPG by private players also dropped sharply, falling 83.8% in October and 97.3% over the first seven months of the financial year. Sales of packed domestic LPG by state-owned companies declined 11.8% in October, while bulk LPG sales recorded a steeper contraction of 49.1%. In contrast, auto LPG sales increased by 23.9%.India’s imports of petroleum products contracted 41.2% in October, taking the decline for the current financial year so far to 49.3%. According to the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), the fall in imports during April-October was driven largely by reduced purchases of LPG, petroleum coke and fuel oil from overseas markets.Indian refineries processed 24.1 million tonnes of crude oil in October, marking a 7.1% increase and equivalent to approximately 5.70 million barrels per day. Imported crude accounted for 22 million tonnes of the total, while domestic production contributed 2.1 million tonnes. Imports covered 88.7% of the country’s crude oil consumption during the month.Domestic production of crude oil and condensate stood at 2.3 million tonnes. Meanwhile, India’s dependence on imports to meet natural gas requirements was 52.8% in October.
Article Summary: Petrol and diesel prices in India had risen by just 7% over a four-year reference period. This is significantly less than the increase of 50-70% recorded in other parts of the world. Oil minister credited the relatively limited rise to three reductions in central excise duty and the role of oil marketing companies.

Article Title: COP31 climate talks collapse: What Saudi Arabia, Iran & Russia opposed & why it matters
Article Text:
How COP31 collapsed over fossil fuels

Fossil fuel language becomes central sticking point

Saudi Arabia's influence and questions over negotiations

Climate finance and carbon capture deepen divisions

Why the failure matters as the 1.5°C threshold slips out of reach

COP31 records progress on separate initiatives

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The United Nations climate negotiations at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an overarching agreement on Sunday, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and carbon capture technology preventing nearly 200 countries from reaching a consensus.The failure came after two weeks of negotiations that continued for more than 50 hours beyond their scheduled conclusion, making the summit the longest-ever United Nations climate conference. It was the first time since the 2009 Copenhagen climate summit (COP15) that countries failed to reach a final overarching agreement.While the European Union and several climate-vulnerable nations opposed a final draft that made no mention of fossil fuels, oil-producing countries, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, resisted language calling for a transition away from coal, oil and natural gas.The breakdown came despite efforts by Turkey and Australia, which jointly led the negotiations, to secure an agreement. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed disappointment, warning that delays in climate action would make efforts to tackle global warming increasingly difficult and costly.“I am deeply disappointed that COP31 has ended without consensus on an overarching outcome,” Guterres said.“Temperatures keep shattering records. Climate extremes keep intensifying. Emissions remain far too high. And every delay makes our task harder and more costly.”The biggest disagreement centred on whether the final agreement should explicitly refer to fossil fuels and the need to transition away from them.The draft proposed by the Turkish-Australian leadership did not mention fossil fuels, prompting opposition from the European Union, the United Kingdom, Norway, Canada, Panama, Vanuatu and a group of least developed countries.Several countries had sought to reinforce the commitment made at COP28 in Dubai three years ago to "transitioning away from fossil fuels" and translate it into concrete action.Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking on behalf of the European Union, said the bloc could not support an agreement that failed to acknowledge the role of fossil fuels in driving climate change.“It’s unconscionable that we would have a climate act that makes no reference to fossil fuels,” O'Brien said.The EU also warned that the proposed text fell short of the scientific requirements for addressing the climate crisis and risked legitimising continued fossil fuel use.Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Iran and Russia opposed including language on fossil fuels. Russia's representative said, “We cannot agree to any wording on fossil fuels.”Saudi Arabia also defended the inclusion of carbon capture technologies, arguing that they should remain among the options available to address climate change while allowing continued oil and gas production.The draft's explicit language and targets for carbon capture and storage for industrial polluters further complicated the negotiations. Several countries and environmental groups argued that the approach could undermine efforts to reduce overall emissions.Former US Vice President Al Gore criticised the outcome, saying, “The failure of COP31 is an outrage — it is outrageous that a handful of petrostates have veto power over any mention of fossil fuels."Saudi Arabia's role in the negotiations came under scrutiny, with negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa alleging that the country had disproportionate access to the conference leadership.According to the negotiators, Saudi officials had regular access to the Turkish and Australian presidents of the talks, while a promised meeting with the leadership for a representative of a small island state was repeatedly cancelled as the conference went into extended overtime.Riyadh was at the forefront of efforts to resist language on reducing reliance on fossil fuels, the negotiators said, adding that this was a key reason an agreement could not be reached.Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking on behalf of the European Union, said, "This COP, I believe, was hijacked by some oil states."The Turkish COP presidency rejected allegations of preferential access, saying in a statement that no group or country had received "preferential treatment". Representatives for Saudi Arabia and Australia did not immediately comment.Saudi Arabia and other members of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) have long opposed climate language targeting fossil fuels, arguing that they will remain part of the global energy mix for the foreseeable future.Negotiators also said Riyadh's position was strengthened by the absence of active US engagement at COP31 and the lack of close US-China coordination, which had helped broker compromises at previous climate summits."Instead of having one or two major players helping define the boundaries of the discussion, those boundaries have become less clear," Singapore Environment Minister Grace Fu said.Disagreements over financial assistance for developing countries also contributed to the failure to reach consensus.Developing nations argued that the proposed agreement did not provide adequate financial support to help them adapt to rising temperatures and increasingly extreme weather events.The Philippines delegation stressed that financial commitments needed to be backed by resources for mitigation, adaptation, technology transfer, capacity building and efforts to address loss and damage."Climate finance must be fully mobilized to drive needed scale and speed in mitigation, adaptation, technology transfer, capacity building and loss and damage," the delegation said."A target without means is a promise without a pathway."The negotiations also failed to resolve differences over the details of transitioning away from fossil fuels and climate-related gender action, with several issues deferred to next year's discussions in Ethiopia.The collapse of the negotiations comes at a critical juncture in global climate action. The United Nations has warned that the world is set to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius warming threshold established under the 2015 Paris Agreement.The threshold refers to limiting long-term global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Beyond this level, the risks and intensity of extreme weather events, including heatwaves, floods and droughts, increase.Scientists estimate that the world is currently heading towards warming of between 2.7 and 3 degrees Celsius by the end of the century.Without an overarching agreement, countries failed to secure fresh collective commitments on key issues, including moving away from fossil fuels and providing financial assistance to developing nations facing the effects of climate change.The negotiations also took place against the backdrop of an energy crisis linked to the war in Iran, economic pressures and competing geopolitical priorities, which further complicated efforts to build consensus.Guterres said continued dependence on fossil fuels was worsening the climate crisis and exposing economies to energy price shocks.“The continued addiction to coal, oil and gas is fueling climate chaos, exposing economies to price shocks and undermining energy security. We can’t put out the fire while pouring fuel on it,” he said.Despite the failure to reach an overarching agreement, the summit saw progress on several separate initiatives.Turkey had made global electrification one of its key priorities for the conference. A separate proposal called on countries to increase the share of electricity in total final energy consumption from around 21 per cent currently to 35 per cent by 2035. Nearly 100 countries signed up to the pledge.The target would require countries to expand the use of electricity in sectors such as transport and industry, including shifting cars, trucks and planes away from fossil fuels and replacing coal with electricity in industrial production.Several other measures were agreed upon, including a pledge on a just transition for workers and communities dependent on fossil fuels. Progress was also reported on global adaptation goals and a programme to help countries implement emissions-reduction targets fairly.However, these separate initiatives could not make up for the absence of a comprehensive agreement.Manuel Pulgar-Vidal, president of COP20 and climate and energy lead at the World Wildlife Fund, said the summit had left major issues unresolved.“COP31 left too much undone,” he said.“Too many once again shied away from the toughest decisions, including how to turn their commitment to transition away from fossil fuels into real action. The climate will not wait for governments to find their courage.”
Article Summary: The United Nations climate negotiations at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an overarching agreement on Sunday. The failure came after two weeks of negotiations that continued for more than 50 hours beyond their scheduled conclusion. It was the first time since the 2009 Copenhagen climate summit (COP15) that countries failed to reach a final overarching agreement.

Article Title: Gurgaon man waits 22 years for commercial plot bought at MCG auction in 2004, consumer commission orders civic body to hand over possession and pay Rs 72,000
Article Text:
(AI Image) The allotment letter was issued on June 17, 2004.





GURGAON: Holding that a civic body cannot penalise an auction purchaser for delayed payments when possession of the property remains uncertain due to litigation and lack of development, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed the Municipal Corporation of Gurgaon (MCG) to hand over a commercial plot, execute its conveyance deed and pay Rs 72,000 to the buyer.The commission also ordered MCG to waive interest, if any, on delayed instalments attributable to the period during which a court stay was in force. It held that the civic body had committed a severe deficiency in service by failing to deliver possession of the property despite receiving the full sale consideration.The order was passed on a complaint filed by Sachin Malik, who purchased plot No. 39, measuring 91.87 square metres, at Vyapar Sadan shopping complex through a public auction in February 2004. The allotment letter was issued on June 17, 2004.Malik initially deposited Rs 2.35 lakh, or 10% of the auction value. He was subsequently asked to deposit another Rs 3.52 lakh within 30 days. However, the plot became embroiled in litigation, with a civil court directing the parties to maintain status quo on construction and possession in March 2004. The order remained in force until June 2009.The commission noted that Malik had repeatedly approached MCG during this period, seeking possession or an alternative plot, but received no response.It also observed that the civic body had failed to adequately develop the auction site for more than a decade after the allotment.The order was passed by commission president Sanjeev Jindal and members Jyoti Siwach and Khushwinder Kaur. The commission said an allottee could not reasonably be expected to continue depositing instalments when the delivery of possession was uncertain and dependent on the outcome of pending litigation. It held that Malik could not be faulted for withholding instalments under such circumstances or be made liable to pay penal interest.The civic body's defence that auction purchasers were not consumers under the Consumer Protection Act was also rejected. The commission said consumer jurisdiction could be invoked in cases where a public authority failed to deliver possession because of court stays, unresolved disputes or other complications. It also accepted Malik's assertion that he had purchased the commercial plot for his livelihood through self-employment, bringing the transaction within the ambit of consumer protection law.MCG had further argued that the complaint was time-barred, as the last payment had been encashed in April 2020 and the complaint was filed in April 2026. The commission rejected this contention, observing that the amount had not been refunded and the continued failure to hand over possession gave the buyer a continuing cause of action.The commission directed MCG to hand over possession of the plot, issue a possession certificate, and execute and register the conveyance deed. It also awarded Rs 50,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 22,000 towards litigation expenses.The civic body has been directed to comply within 45 days of the order becoming operative. Failure to pay the awarded amount would attract annual interest of 12%, while non-compliance could lead to execution proceedings and prosecution under the Consumer Protection Act.
Article Summary: Sachin Malik purchased plot No. 39, measuring 91.87 square metres, at a public auction in February 2004. The allotment letter was issued on June 17, 2004. plot became embroiled in litigation, with a civil court directing the parties to maintain status quo on construction and possession in March 2004.

Amid the ongoing record rally, Indian equity benchmarks snapped their winning streak to crash in trade on Monday. BSE Sensex and Nifty50 both plunged over 1.5% as profit booking and global cues led to a slide.Weakness also spread to the broader market, with the Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap 250 indices slipping into negative territory.BSE Sensex ended the day at 82,435.99, down 1,4584 points or 1.77%. Nifty50 closed at 25,349.65, down 451 points or 1.75%. The crash wiped out over Rs 6.39 lakh crore of investors’ wealth, with market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies dropping to Rs 508 lakh crore.Among Sensex constituents, Tata Steel, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India (SBI) and UltraTech Cement dropped by as much as 6%. In contrast, TCS, Tech Mahindra, Infosys, HCL Tech and Maruti Suzuki were among the stocks trading higher.The biggest reason is profit booking that has emerged after the recent record breaking run of stocks. Nifty has gained more than 10% and is on course to deliver its best monthly performance since 2020, prompting investors to lock in gains after the sharp rise.Indian equities are approaching their previous record highs, supported by a turnaround in foreign institutional investor (FII) flows that has significantly altered market sentiment.The Nifty 50 is now just over 2% below its lifetime high of 26,373.20, while the Sensex is less than 3% away from its record peak of 86,159.Expectations of tighter US monetary policy have returned to the forefront, with markets assigning a 93% probability to an interest rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December policy meeting, according to CME's FedWatch tool.The Fed's interest rate outlook also remains an important driver of bullion prices. On Friday, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook supported further rate increases, arguing that the prevailing policy rate was not high enough to tackle inflation, which she said she viewed with "great concern".A rate increase by the US central bank can make American investments more attractive relative to Indian equities.The Indian rupee weakened sharply and was heading towards the 93-per-dollar level after briefly moving above 92.50. The currency had closed at 92.67 on Friday.A weaker rupee raises the domestic cost of imports, particularly crude oil, increasing expenses for Indian businesses and adding to inflationary pressures. It can also erode the dollar-denominated returns earned by overseas investors, making Indian equities less attractive and potentially prompting further FPI selling.Several of the market's biggest constituents, including HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India (SBI) and Axis Bank, declined by as much as 2.5% on Monday, adding to the pressure on benchmark indices.The impact of these declines on the Nifty is amplified by the index's market capitalisation-based weighting system.Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited says, “Last week’s late global sell-off, triggered by concerns over an AI bubble and tighter US monetary policy, weighed on Indian equities today. Selling was concentrated in heavyweight banking and commodity stocks amid weak FII sentiment.The domestic market also remains vulnerable to profit booking after the recent sharp rally and a holiday-shortened week. Mixed Asian markets and a positive European opening helped limit losses. The outlook hinges on whether the AI-led sell-off remains contained. Although valuations have corrected significantly, concerns over the sustainability of debt-funded data-centre investments continue to weigh on global sentiment. Further weakness in global equities could spill over into India, though the impact may be relatively limited given India’s lower exposure to AI-driven investment and resilient domestic economy. Improving manufacturing activity and expectations of robust Q2 GDP growth of ~7.7% remain key fundamental supports for a constructive medium- to long-term outlook."
Article Summary: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 both plunged over 1.5% as profit booking and global cues led to a slide. Selling was concentrated in heavyweight banking and commodity stocks. Indian equities are approaching their previous record highs, supported by a turnaround in foreign institutional investor (FII) flows.

Article Title: India's ageing Barak missile shield gets Rs 1,976 crore upgrade: What changes
Article Text:

The defence ministry has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgradation and obsolescence management of the Barak point defence missile system fitted on Indian warships. Under the deal, IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software, which the ministry says will give naval platforms enhanced features and a potent anti-air defence capability.The announcement stresses capability, but obsolescence management is arguably the heart of the contract. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades on Delhi-class destroyers, Shivalik-class and Brahmaputra-class frigates and the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya. Many of its electronic components, processors and sensors are now ageing, and in several cases the original manufacturers no longer produce spares, making readiness increasingly expensive to sustain.Two practical considerations explain the need for modernisation of the point defence system. Replacing every installation would cost far more and disrupt operations more than upgrading systems already integrated into the fleet, and many of these ships will serve for years. DRDO 's indigenous VL-SRSAM is meant to succeed the Barak-1, but fleet-wide induction will take time.The upgrade ensures no capability gap in the interim. Better software, computing power and fire-control can improve reaction time, reliability, availability and resistance to jamming, even if the missile itself remains the same.The deal also underlines why point-defence systems matter. They form the last layer of an integrated air-defence network, protecting specific assets such as ships, airbases, radars and command centres against threats that slip past outer defences. On a warship, the Barak-1 is that final missile layer against aircraft, drones and anti-ship missiles. Warships are also equipped with gun based close in weapon systems such as the AK-630 which form the final line of defence.Cheap drones, loitering munitions and faster, low-flying missiles shorten reaction time, while the Russia-Ukraine conflict has shown how massed drones can be used against airbases and logistics hubs.Using costly long-range interceptors against inexpensive drones is an unfavourable trade, so shorter-range systems help conserve missiles for graver threats. The danger is saturation, where a defender runs out of interceptors even after intercepting everything.For India, with airbases and forward positions spread along the northern and western borders, layered cover is essential. DRDO's VSHORADS cleared three flight trials on February 27 this year, and the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System, combining QRSAM, VSHORADS and a laser-based weapon, had its maiden trials on August 23, 2025. The Defence Acquisition Council cleared VSHORADS and medium-range missile procurement for the Army on July 3.The Barak contract is thus less a missile purchase than a sustainment effort. It also reinforces the India-Israel defence partnership, which includes the jointly developed Barak-8.
Article Summary: India has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries. IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades.
